findings.text: A threaded stress routine coordinates a worker group through a shared startup barrier, tolerates individual spawn failures, collects per-worker completion status, releases shared structures, then runs a reduced secondary table check and reports aggregate started, failed and secondary outcome.

Startup uses an atomic counter observed at zero via a wait queue, followed by a final decrement below zero and a broadcast wake so surviving workers proceed together; failed spawns adjust the counter without joining the group.
The secondary table exercise uses one sixteenth of the primary entry count to bound its cost, reflecting that its removal path is disproportionately expensive.
Base fixtures provide eight branch controls spanning older and newer declaration forms, each with true and false initial states and a companion copy that load-time logic flips to the opposite state.

A branch test record combines an expected boolean, a reference to a branch control, and a parameterless probe of branch outcome, enabling direct state and helper results to be judged against one expectation.

Branch validation checks a mixed table of local and external controls against expected states, flips each distinct control and rechecks against inverted expectations, then restores and rechecks original expectations, failing on any disagreement between stored state, expectation, or probe.
Inversion is a pure toggle with no third state, applied once per distinct control address when processing a table.
Base module load flips its inverted companions while unload is inert; the main branch test performs full validation during load and is inert at unload.

Sysctl test storage groups scalar integers, a four-element integer vector, a boot integer, an unsigned integer, a short string buffer, a bitmap pointer, plus separate bound and match flag variables with documented defaults.

Table entries bind a name to storage, byte length, access mode, vector handler, and optional limit references, covering integer, unsigned, string and large bitmap kinds with read-only reporting for the match flag.

Sysctl self test progresses through constant validation with bitmap allocation, nested registration with immediate unregister, mount point creation with a nested entry that must not attach, empty directory layering, and unsigned range checks where invalid limits must be rejected and a valid range must be accepted.
Sysctl unload frees the bitmap storage and unregisters each populated header slot while skipping empty slots.
A global match flag begins true and is cleared permanently if any reference constant differs from its expected numeric value, surfacing constant corruption through a single readable entry.
Large bitmap extent is 65536 with byte allocation as one eighth of that extent.
String capacity is 65, integer vector length is 4, and the header registry provides 6 usable slots with a seventh enumerator serving as size marker.
Writable entries use mode 0644 and the match entry uses 0444; integer limits use 0 and 100 while unsigned trials use 4 to 1000 as over, -1 to 100 as under, and 0 to 200 as valid.
Log output from the sysctl test prefixes each message with the module name and a separator.

Sanitizer probes are parameterless procedures held in a main table iterated at load and a separate retained table holding a divide probe excluded from automatic iteration; a logging helper records the probe name and whether its configuration is enabled.

Probes deliberately exercise distinct fault classes including integer wrapping and negation, truncation, out-of-range shifts, indexes beyond either end cushioned by guard storage, invalid boolean and enumeration payloads, and an unaligned store.
Sanitizer load executes each main table entry and reports success while unload does nothing; the retained divide probe is never executed automatically.
Concurrent completion is tracked by an atomic outstanding count whose final transition to zero signals a global completion object exactly once.

Allocation coverage spans randomized size with randomized alignment, exhaustive single-bit alignment sweep, fixed large alignment, randomized page counts with access touch, a large persistent busy set interleaved with transient large and small allocations, reuse of freed holes sized from processor count, fixed counts with optional huge backing, and non-blocking allocations under disabled preemption.
Allocation helpers treat null returns as failures, release transient and tracking buffers on examined paths, and surface a negative status without proceeding to use the missing block.
A declaration helper introduces a static variable with an initial value and publishes it as a read-only module parameter with descriptive text.
